Prepare Data for TNA Analysis

Source: R/data_conversion.R
prepare_for_tna.Rd

prepare_for_tna() returns the sequence columns of a data set as a wide data frame for tna::tna() and related functions: one row per sequence and the position columns V1, V2, ... in numeric order, with factors turned into character. Long input is converted with long_to_wide() first, padding shorter sequences with NA. Every other column (an id, metadata) is dropped.

Usage

prepare_for_tna(
  data,
  type = c("sequences", "long", "auto"),
  state_names = NULL,
  id_col = "Actor",
  time_col = "Time",
  action_col = "Action",
  validate = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of sequences: wide, with position columns named V1, V2, ..., or long, with one row per action.

type

How to read data. "sequences" (default) reads wide position columns; "long" converts a long table with long_to_wide(), which needs id_col and action_col; "auto" reads long data when action_col is a column and no V<number> column exists, wide data in the opposite case, and, when both exist, long data only if id_col is a column and there are more than twice as many rows as ids. Data with neither raises an error. Whatever the type, the result needs V<number> columns; others, such as T1, T2, are not renamed and raise an error.

state_names

The expected states, used with validate. Default NULL, which accepts the states found in the data.

id_col

The column identifying sequences in long data. Default "Actor".

time_col

The column ordering the actions in long data. Default "Time".

action_col

The column holding the actions in long data. Default "Action".

validate

Whether to check the states against state_names; states not listed are named in a warning. Ignored when state_names is NULL. Default TRUE.

Value

A data frame with one row per sequence and only the position columns V1, V2, ..., in numeric order, holding character states (or the original type for non-factor columns), with no row names.

See also

wide_to_long, long_to_wide for format conversions.

Examples

# From wide format sequences
sequences <- data.frame(
  V1 = c("A","B","C","A"), V2 = c("B","C","A","B"),
  V3 = c("C","A","B","C"), V4 = c("A","B","A","B")
)
tna_data <- prepare_for_tna(sequences, type = "sequences")
